why_adversarial: This French marriage certificate has two compounding adversarial properties: (a) the first page is entirely missing — the document title 'ACTE DE MARIAGE' and the mairie header are not present; (b) the scan starts mid-page 2, cutting off the top 40%, which removes the mayor's full signature, the witnesses' names, and the acte number suffix. A classifier must infer MARRIAGE_CERTIFICATE from the remaining mid-document text alone — specifically the civil ceremony language ('Le mariage a été célébré'), the two-party 'entre: ... et ...' structure, the célibataire status declarations, and the Code Civil reference. A weak classifier may emit BIRTH_CERTIFICATE (confused by birth dates and parental names) or UNKNOWN (due to the missing header).
classifier_failure_mode: Classifier emits BIRTH_CERTIFICATE because the text contains multiple 'né le' (born on) entries, parental names, and place-of-birth references — all of which also appear in birth certificates. Missing document header eliminates the easiest classification signal. Secondary failure: UNKNOWN due to truncated scan.
gold_signals_expected: Le mariage a été célébré — explicit marriage ceremony language
Two-party structure: Monsieur X ... et Madame Y ... (bride and groom)
Célibataire status for both parties — pre-marriage civil status
Officier d'état civil / Le Maire references — French civil registry authority
notes: The né le entries refer to the spouses' birth dates (biographical fields within the marriage act), NOT birth certificates. The two-person 'entre... et...' ceremony structure is the strongest discriminating signal for MARRIAGE_CERTIFICATE vs BIRTH_CERTIFICATE. The Code Civil reference and mairie cachet are secondary confirmatory signals. Confidence below 0.80 is correct given the missing page-1 header — escalation is the right path. The cross-national element (French husband, Moroccan wife) is incidental but realistic.
